title: Synthesis Phase Subsumes Its Epistemic Gate
summary: Establishes that the synthesis phase does not add a separate epistemic gate after its outline deliverable; instead the three-phase conversation (ADR-013) itself subsumes the gate function — Journey Review requires retrieval and articulation, Novelty Surfacing requires reflection and self-explanation, and the Framing Conversation requires articulation and generation. The synthesis essay, written outside the pipeline, is the terminal epistemic act of the entire RDD cycle, satisfying Invariant 1 at its highest level, while Invariant 2 is satisfied because every conversational step is generative rather than mere approval. This resolves the domain model's open question of whether synthesis needs its own gate.
workflow_point: synthesis phase gate — resolved as none needed, subsumed by the conversation
mechanism: three conversation phases mapped to specific epistemic acts, with the essay as terminal epistemic act

links.note: Preserves ADR-002's principle that each skill owns its gate: the synthesis skill's gate is its own conversation structure, not a separate bolt-on.
ADR-003's pattern of assigning specific epistemic-act types to gates applies implicitly: the three conversation phases map to retrieval, reflection, articulation, and self-explanation.
The three-phase conversation structure defined in ADR-013 is reinterpreted here as also fulfilling the epistemic-gate function, rather than requiring a separate gate.
